concepts.label: User-Defined Functions UI (Web Console Query > UDF screen)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - a UI-specific concept for the management surface itself, per the batch instructions' explicit steer to decide per-fact whether it belongs to the existing js-udf: family or to the UI surface. The page is entirely about the console screen (create/update/delete UDFs and libraries); every underlying JS-UDF concept it touches (library, inline function, external function, sql-managed UDF) is reused from the already-promoted js-udf: family below rather than re-described here

concepts.label: JavaScript UDF library
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - promoted. The page's 'JavaScript Function Libraries' section is this UI's create/edit/drop surface for the concept

concepts.label: Inline user-defined function (defined using SQL++ expressions, no external library)
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - extraction-layer, minted in cloud/javascript-udfs/javascript-functions-with-couchbase.json. The UI's 'Inline' function-type row ('a function written in SQL++ which can be used as part of another SQL++ statement') is this same SQL++-expression-only concept, not the broader class that includes sql-managed JavaScript - checked against the concept's own recorded evidence ('An inline SQL++ function is a user-defined function that executes a SQL++ expression') before reusing rather than minting a UI-specific duplicate

concepts.label: External (library-backed) JavaScript UDF
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - promoted. The UI's 'JavaScript' function-type row ('You can create SQL++ functions that call the JavaScript functions defined in your library') is exactly this concept: a SQL++ function referencing a named function inside a js-udf:udf-library

concepts.label: SQL++ managed JavaScript UDF
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - promoted. The page's own closing NOTE names this concept by definition ('JavaScript functions which are not stored in a library') specifically to state that the UI does NOT support creating it - see the doesNotSupport relation below

relations.subject: js-udf:udf-library
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted, same predicate/shape already recorded for js-udf:udf-library createdVia tool:query-workbench in server/8.0/javascript-udfs/javascript-functions-with-couchbase.json - this UI is a second, distinct creation surface for the same concept
relations.evidence: Click on the `+ add function library` link to create a library of JavaScript functions.

relations.subject: js-udf:inline-function
relations.evidence: If you are defining an `inline` function then you can fill in any valid SQL++ expression which can then be used as part of another SQL++ statement. This is the default when creating a function.

relations.subject: js-udf:external-function
relations.evidence: If you switch **Function Type** to `javascript` then the dialog will change to configure a JavaScript function call.

relations.subject: tool:udfs-ui
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate ('a stated, bounded non-support boundary'), same shape already used for tool:cbcollect-info's audit-log/Eventing-log exclusions per the registry digest
relations.evidence: You cannot use the UDF console to create SQL++ managed user-defined functions — that is, JavaScript functions which are not stored in a library. To do this, see [CREATE FUNCTION](../n1ql/n1ql-language-reference/createfunction.md).

relations.subject: server/8.0/tools/udfs-ui
